cls: Antineoplastic - highly selective RET kinase inhibitor
pharm: Selective rearranged during transfection (RET) kinase inhibitor; blocks RET fusion and mutant signaling to inhibit tumor cell proliferation in RET-driven cancers
quick: 400 mg orally once daily on an empty stomach
Empty stomach: no food for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after the dose
Can cause fetal harm; avoid - use effective nonhormonal contraception
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
No adjustment in mild impairment; not established in moderate-severe
No adjustment in mild impairment; not established in moderate-severe
No specific interaction; limit due to hepatic and GI effects
Blood pressure, LFTs, pulmonary symptoms, bleeding, wound healing, pregnancy status
summary: Pralsetinib (Gavreto) is a highly selective RET kinase inhibitor for RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer. It potently inhibits RET fusions and resistance-relevant RET alterations while sparing most off-target kinases. The adult dose is 400 mg orally once daily taken on an empty stomach. Major serious risks include interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, hypertension, hepatotoxicity, hemorrhagic events, tumor lysis syndrome, impaired wound healing, and embryo-fetal toxicity. It is a CYP3A and P-gp substrate with dose adjustments for interacting drugs.
indications: Treatment of adult patients with metastatic RET fusion-positive NSCLC

Treatment of adult and pediatric patients 12 years and older with advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer who require systemic therapy and who are radioactive iodine-refractory (if radioactive iodine is appropriate)

dosage.c: Standard adult dose (RET fusion-positive NSCLC or thyroid cancer)
dosage.t: Once daily on an empty stomach
dosage.n: Continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; confirm RET fusion before starting

dosage.d: First reduction 300 mg once daily, then 200 mg once daily, then 100 mg once daily
dosage.n: Permanently discontinue if unable to tolerate 100 mg once daily

dosage.c: With strong CYP3A inhibitor or combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitor
dosage.d: Reduce current dose (400 mg to 200 mg; 300 mg to 200 mg; 200 mg to 100 mg once daily)
dosage.n: Resume prior dose 3 to 5 half-lives after stopping the inhibitor; avoid combination where possible

dosage.d: Increase current dose (400 mg to 600 mg; 300 mg to 500 mg; 200 mg to 300 mg once daily)
dosage.n: Resume prior dose 7 to 14 days after stopping the inducer; avoid combination where possible

admin: Take 400 mg by mouth once daily on an empty stomach with no food for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after the dose
Swallow capsules whole with water; do not crush, chew, or open
Take at about the same time each day; confirm RET fusion status with a validated test before starting
Withhold for at least 5 days before elective surgery and for at least 2 weeks after major surgery until wounds heal; safety of resuming after wound complications is not established
Monitor blood pressure, liver tests, pulmonary status, and bleeding during treatment
moa: Pralsetinib is a potent, selective inhibitor of rearranged during transfection (RET) kinase, including oncogenic RET fusions and activating RET mutations. By occupying the ATP-binding pocket of RET, it blocks autophosphorylation and downstream signaling through MAPK and PI3K/AKT pathways, inhibiting proliferation and survival of RET-driven tumor cells. It has activity against predicted gatekeeper resistance variants and relative selectivity over VEGFR and other kinases, which shapes its toxicity profile.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to pralsetinib or any excipient
relative: Prior or active interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis
Active significant bleeding risk or recent hemoptysis
Recent major surgery or unhealed wounds
Tumor at high risk of lysis (bulky or rapidly proliferative disease)
monitor: Tumor lysis labs (uric acid, electrolytes, renal function)

preg: Based on mechanism and animal data, pralsetinib can cause fetal harm including malformations and embryolethality at exposures below the human 400 mg dose. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: There are no data on pralsetinib in human milk or its effects on the breastfed child or milk production. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the final dose.
renal: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild renal impairment. Pralsetinib has not been adequately studied in moderate to severe renal impairment; use with caution and monitor closely for toxicity.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended for mild hepatic impairment. Pralsetinib has not been adequately studied in moderate to severe hepatic impairment; use with caution with close monitoring of liver tests and adverse reactions.

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - increase pralsetinib exposure; reduce pralsetinib dose
Combined P-gp and strong CYP3A inhibitors (e.g., itraconazole) - increase exposure; reduce pralsetinib dose
Strong CYP3A inducers (e.g., rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, St John's wort) - decrease exposure and efficacy; avoid, or increase pralsetinib dose if unavoidable
moderate: Moderate CYP3A inducers - may reduce exposure; monitor efficacy
Agents that increase bleeding risk (anticoagulants, antiplatelets, NSAIDs) - additive hemorrhage risk; monitor closely
minor: Acid-reducing agents - no major interaction described; maintain empty-stomach dosing
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach; food increases exposure and toxicity risk. No food for at least 2 hours before and at least 1 hour after dosing.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol because of hepatotoxicity and bleeding risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor ALT/AST, blood pressure, and tumor lysis labs (potassium, uric acid, phosphate, calcium, creatinine); evaluate new pulmonary infiltrates.

serious: Hemorrhagic events including severe and fatal hemorrhage
rare: Pneumocystis pneumonia and other severe infections in clinical experience
Severe cutaneous reactions reported with RET inhibitor class
emergency: New or worsening dyspnea, cough, or fever (possible pneumonitis) - seek urgent evaluation
Severe headache, chest pain, or neurologic symptoms (hypertensive crisis)
Active bleeding, hemoptysis, hematuria, or melena
Oliguria with nausea, muscle cramps, or palpitations (tumor lysis syndrome)

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline, after 1 week, then at least monthly
Liver function (ALT, AST) at baseline, every 2 weeks for the first 3 months, then monthly
Pulmonary symptoms and imaging for ILD/pneumonitis; withhold for new respiratory symptoms
Complete blood count and tumor lysis labs in high-risk patients
Pregnancy status before starting; bleeding and wound healing around procedures
counsel: Take on a completely empty stomach: nothing to eat for 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose, at the same time daily
Report new cough, shortness of breath, or fever right away (possible lung inflammation)
Report unusual bleeding, coughing or vomiting blood, black stools, or blood in urine
Tell your team about scheduled surgery or dental procedures; you will need to pause treatment around surgery for wound healing
Use effective nonhormonal birth control during treatment and for 2 weeks after the last dose (partners: 1 week for males); do not breastfeed
Tell your doctor about all medicines including antifungals, antibiotics, seizure drugs, herbal products, and blood thinners
pk: Target inhibition within hours of dosing; radiographic responses typically develop over weeks
Median Tmax about 2 to 4 hours after oral dosing on an empty stomach
Mean elimination half-life about 15 to 22 hours, supporting once-daily dosing
Steady state within about 1 week of once-daily dosing
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); protect from moisture in original container
pearls: Confirm RET fusion with a validated test before starting; active in both NSCLC and RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer
Empty-stomach dosing is strict (2 hours before, 1 hour after) because food raises exposure
Withhold at least 5 days before elective surgery and at least 2 weeks after major surgery until wounds heal
ILD/pneumonitis, hypertension, hepatotoxicity, hemorrhage, and tumor lysis syndrome drive dose holds and reductions (400 to 300 to 200 to 100 mg)
CYP3A/P-gp substrate: reduce dose with strong CYP3A or combined P-gp/strong CYP3A inhibitors; increase dose if a strong inducer cannot be avoided
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible on the same day. Resume the regular schedule the next day. Do not take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed dose. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not take an extra dose; take the next dose at the regular time.
overdose: There is no specific antidote for pralsetinib overdose. Expected effects reflect exaggerated toxicities including hypertension, hepatotoxicity, cytopenias, hemorrhage, and pneumonitis. Withhold drug, provide supportive care with blood pressure control, liver and pulmonary monitoring, blood counts, and bleeding management. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
